# FoodGauge

> FoodGauge is a free food label scanner for iPhone (Android in closed testing on Google Play). Scan a barcode, or photograph the ingredient label when a product has no record, to see ingredients, allergens, additives, E codes and available nutrition information, with the source of each fact. No account is needed.

Site: https://teach-bot-sys.github.io/foodgauge-site/
App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6802302665
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/food.gauge/
Contact: mrfatihkrkmz@gmail.com
Publisher: Kaira Labs
Platforms: iOS (live), Android (closed testing)
Price: Free, contains ads
App languages: English, Turkish, Spanish, French, Russian, Arabic
Site languages: English, Turkish, Russian, Arabic

## How it works

1. Scan a barcode or type it in. FoodGauge shows the ingredients and nutrition information it can find in community product records, together with where each fact came from. Barcode lookups need an internet connection.
2. When a product has no record, or no barcode, photograph the ingredient label or choose an image from the gallery. The text is read on the phone, and the user can review and correct it before it is used.
3. Allergens the user flags in Settings are highlighted. Additives are recognised by E code or by name. Contains and may-contain declarations are shown separately.

## Evidence before scores

- Most products open with an "At a glance" card instead of an overall health score: the user's allergens, the number of additives, and sugar, saturated fat and salt amounts.
- When the evidence required for a score is unavailable, the score is withheld. Missing or conflicting information stays visible.
- Saved products and recent inspections can be reopened, and facts can be compared when a valid common measurement basis is available.

## Halal, vegan and vegetarian

For barcodes, halal, vegan and vegetarian status from community databases is shown and marked as not a certification. The ingredient list is also checked on the phone for related words, and the words found are shown. These are clues, not certifications.

## Offline use

Basic Mode reads labels on the device and includes a local E-code catalog, so it works without internet. New barcode lookups require a connection.

## Privacy

- No account, registration or personal profile.
- The camera is used only after the user chooses to take a photo. The photo picker receives only the selected image.
- Label text is read on the phone with OCR. In AI mode, only the extracted text is sent for analysis; the photo is not uploaded.
- A barcode lookup sends the barcode number to fetch the product record.
- Scan history is stored on the device and can be deleted record by record or cleared entirely.
- The app shows ads; ad personalisation follows the consent choice made on first launch, which can be revisited from the privacy screen.
- No medical profile, diet profile or health record is created or requested.

## Limitations

FoodGauge provides general label information. It is not medical advice or a personalised nutrition plan. Source records do not replace the current package; users should check the label itself for allergy-related decisions. FoodGauge does not use Nutri-Score branding and is not affiliated with any food authority.
